newFacts: The current official NIRCam calibration documentation and the August 2026 primary preprint supersede the older calibration state used in early JWST work.
Program 6605 provides three public hot standards with exactly four in-footprint CAL exposures per F090W/F150W target-detector group at the sampled anchors.
The simple r=5 operator passes support, central DQ, and robust-scatter gates but fails the registered F090W excursion and cross-star replication gates.
Program 7565 already has public F090W/F150W observations of two different Cycle 4 hot standards, enabling a fresh future holdout.
changedProblemStates: UP-003 advances from 'no external isolated-star test' to 'raw external operator tested and rejected'; its crowded-field, TRGB, distance, and H0 states remain unchanged.
UP-625 gains a concrete matched-support transport statistic, but F090W transfer fails.
UP-626 validates preregistered support-first outcome access and a terminal negative decision with exact independent recomputation.
reproducedOrRejectedApproaches: The official SCI/PHOTMJSR*AREA r=5 aperture core was reproduced on public CAL products, but the simplified operator without the full STPSF/jump/CALSPEC chain was rejected for transfer.
A fixed detector-position correction inferred from the four NRCB1 dither residuals was rejected in F090W because the pattern did not reproduce across standards.
Changing aperture from r=3 to r=8 does not remove the WDFS0458-56 F090W excursion, so aperture size alone is not a supported rescue.
survivingHypotheses: A filter- and exposure-state-specific term, including jump processing or time-dependent PSF aperture fraction, may explain the F090W divergence.
The full official per-image STPSF correction may qualify where the deliberately simplified raw aperture operator failed.
A corrected operator may transfer if developed on retired Program 6605 data and tested once on the new Program 7565 standards.
minimumDecisiveNextTest: On retired Program 6605 only, compare the registered raw result with the official jump-aware and per-image STPSF aperture-corrected branches. Freeze the winning branch and all thresholds before reading Program 7565 WDFS1304+10 and WDFS1557+55 pixels; then repeat the two-filter matched-pattern adjudication once.
insufficientClaims: The current test does not identify whether the F090W failure comes from jump handling, PSF aperture fraction, residual flat field, or epoch/source interaction.
Three local anchors do not characterize detector-wide spatial variation.
No isolated-star result identifies error in crowded-field PSF subtraction, Cepheid photometry, TRGB, distance, or H0.
failuresPreserved: RC72's EE80 support and core-adjudicator failures remain immutable.
RC73's two F090W gate failures remain terminal for the simple raw operator.
nextStart: Inventory Program 7565 products and WCS support without reading pixels. In parallel, use only retired Program 6605 outcomes to lock an official jump/STPSF correction implementation and an uncertainty budget. The first Program 7565 pixel access begins only after both artifacts are hashed.
